result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.local_and_global_consistency()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Predict missing node labels with the local and global consistency method. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L31036-L31105){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.local_and_global_consistency( label_name="label", alpha=0.99, max_iter=30, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Local and global consistency](/assets/graphs/local-and-global-consistency.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense four-node groups, A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, joined by the edge D to E. Only A is labeled red and H blue, shown as badges. Spreading the labels with the normalized adjacency, each node mixing its neighbors' scores with its own start, predicts red (accent color) for A, B, C, D and blue (teal) for E, F, G, H, as the card lists; both seeds keep their labels." width="100%"} Like `harmonic_function()`, this spreads a few known labels (in the node attribute `label_name`) over the network to classify the remaining nodes, but it lets the known labels themselves be smoothed too. Each node's scores mix what its neighbors say (weight `alpha`) with its own initial label (weight `1 - alpha`), using a symmetrically normalized adjacency, so noisy labels can be overruled by a strongly connected neighborhood (Zhou et al., 2004). The graph must be undirected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [label_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["label"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute holding the known labels (default `"label"`). [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.99]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How much each node listens to its neighbors versus its own initial label, between 0 and 1 (default 0.99). [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[30]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of propagation steps (default 30). [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to propagate along edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The predicted label of every node, keyed by node ID. Unlike `harmonic_function()`, a labeled node can receive a different label. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or no node is labeled. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} With $S = D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2}$ and one-hot labels $Y$, $F \leftarrow \alpha S F + (1 - \alpha) Y$ is iterated `max_iter` times from $F = 0$; it converges to $(1 - \alpha)(I - \alpha S)^{-1} Y$. This is NetworkX's `local_and_global_consistency` exactly (exact ties go to the class seen first). ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#372815b4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(list("ABCDEFGH")) g.add_edges( [("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("E", "F"), ("E", "G"), ("E", "H"), ("F", "G"), ("F", "H"), ("G", "H"), ("D", "E")] ) g.set_node_attrs("label", {g.get_id_from_label("A"): "red", g.get_id_from_label("H"): "blue"}) predicted = g.local_and_global_consistency() {g.get_label_from_id(n): label for n, label in predicted.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 'red', 'B': 'red', 'C': 'red', 'D': 'red', 'E': 'blue', 'F': 'blue', 'G': 'blue', 'H': 'blue'} ``` ::: :::
